analysis: The only change in this PR is documentation in docs/reference/protocol-messages.md, head lines 757-765. It adds a paragraph describing how streamed `auto` tool calls span several `inference_response_chunk` frames. Chunks share one `choices[].delta.tool_calls[].index`. The first chunk carries id, type, function.name and an empty arguments string, and later chunks carry argument fragments that the consumer concatenates. The patch changes no code, wire fields, validation, crypto or authorization paths. I read head units :7 and :8 (lines 1-583) as surrounding context. That context covers the endpoint-resumption protocol (strict 4 KiB bounded decoding, socket nonce, single answer on the registered socket), the drain barrier, and the diagnostics and prefix-cache telemetry descriptions. None of it was modified. The new text describes behavior that is already in the doc and already references encrypted chunk delivery via `encrypted_data`. It does not claim any new trust property. It does not touch T-008 (fail-closed encryption), T-041 (prefix cache) or T-053. The text cites `libs/mlx-swift-lm/.../MLXOpenAIService.swift` `streamChatCompletionFrames` and `../architecture/inference.md#streamed-auto-tool-calls`. Neither source was supplied, so I could not check that the described behavior matches the implementation. This is a documentation accuracy question, not a security regression. One unverified contract is whether tool-call fragments are always encrypted along with other chunk content when E2E encryption is active. That depends on provider code outside this batch. I found no concrete regression and no gap in the threat model that this PR creates.
